name: Urali of Idukki
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Varghese & Mathew 2015 classification note surfaced; no grammar/phonology located

sources.citation: PHOIBLE inventory 1796 'Urali (of Idukki)' (RA source), citing Mohanlal 1991
sources.note: 46 segments, no suprasegmentals, stress or tone listed; confirms that PHOIBLE/Glottolog map Mohan Lal 1991 to ural1274.

Nothing on stress; says url is an Irula-related (Iruloid) variety spoken 'in the hills around Idukki in Kerala, and Bargur in Tamil Nadu' (Bargur hills adjoin Mohan Lal's Talamalai/Sathyamangalam field area).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and reference records for ural1274 (refs 455964 Mohanlal 1991; 550638 Varghese & Mathew 2015)
sources.note: No content; Glottolog's 'most extensive descriptions' for ural1274 are only Varghese & Mathew 2015 and Luiz 1962, both graded wordlist_or_less; Mohanlal 1991 is attached with hhtype unknown. Coordinates 10.85N 76.80E.

sources.citation: Sam Mohan Lal. 1991. A Descriptive Analysis of Urali (Speech of a Dravidian Hill Tribe). CIIL Doctoral Dissertations Series 1. Mysore: Central Institute of Indian Languages (Ph.D., University of Mysore, submitted 1981). 268 leaves.
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter 2 Phonology (pp.55-94) covers vocoids/contoids, phonemes, contrasts, distribution, allophones, clusters, then 2.7 Suprasegmental Phonemes (p.88): 'altogether five suprasegmental phonemes... two junctures namely open and close and three terminals namely rising, falling and suspense'; stress/accent is never mentioned (grep of scanned of the whole chapter: no 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence'). Only prosodic remark elsewhere: p.42 'their intonational pattern shows much deviation from that of Tamil and Kannada'. NB: describes the Urali of the Talamalai/Sathyamangalam ranges (Dimba…
